beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Several plugins installed at once — the question isn't which one to manage. It's whether the hand-offs between them are doing real work.

shot.motion_claim: The writer types the naive routing question and corrects it to the real one: keeping hand-offs intentional.

show.event: types 'If I have several plugins installed,'
types '\ndo I have to manage which one Claude uses?'
backspaces 'manage which one Claude uses' → 'keep every hand-off intentional' on the spoken correction

props.text:
If I have several plugins installed,
do I have to manage which one Claude uses?

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion; cream stage with typed text is the show-tell design.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A plugin stack: several domain plugins installed together, all available at once. A hand-off: one domain's output feeding the next domain's input. And routing: Claude's automatic pick of which skills a request needs — no hand-directing required.

show.event: 'plugin stack' lands
'hand-off' lands
'routing' lands

terms.meaning: several domain plugins installed together; Claude draws from all at once
one domain's output feeding directly into the next domain's input
Claude's automatic pick of which skills a request needs; no hand-directing required

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Picture a stack of domain boxes — marketing, sales, research, data, support. Install them and the whole stack is available at once. You don't route anything by hand.

shot.visual_intent: Five labeled isometric domain boxes drop in one by one and settle in a stacked cluster; all their terracotta lights glow simultaneously once the last box lands.
shot.motion_claim: All five boxes light up at once after the last arrives — proving the whole stack is available simultaneously, not one-at-a-time.

show.event: marketing box drops in from above
sales box drops in
research box drops in
data box drops in
support box drops in and settles
all five terracotta lid-lights glow simultaneously
ink label 'plugin stack' settles below the cluster

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): five isometric boxes on a cream stage, one-word labels, voice explains.

beats.narration_text: Ask a marketing question, the marketing box lights up. Change to a sales question mid-conversation, the sales box engages. Claude changes tools as you change subjects — no announcement required.

shot.visual_intent: A small request slip slides in from the left; the marketing box lights and dims; a second slip arrives; the sales box lights; a third slip; the research box lights. Same cluster from B00.
shot.motion_claim: Three different slips light three different boxes — request subject determines routing automatically, no user intervention shown.

show.event: first request slip slides in from left edge
marketing box lights terracotta; slip lands on it
marketing box dims; second slip arrives
sales box lights; slip lands
sales box dims; third slip arrives
research box lights; slip lands

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: three request slips and three boxes on cream stage; the motion is the whole claim.

beats.narration_text: Ask something that spans two domains, and both contribute. Research findings and marketing positioning flow in and merge into one coherent answer — a whole team's coverage in a single voice.

shot.visual_intent: Research box on the left and marketing box on the right each emit a stream of small blocks toward the center, where they converge and assemble into one output block labeled 'one answer'.
shot.motion_claim: Two separate streams merging into one block — showing that two domain plugins produce a single coordinated output.

show.event: research box emits stream of blocks leftward toward center
marketing box emits stream of blocks rightward toward center
streams meet at center; output block assembles from both
label 'one answer' settles on the assembled block in ink

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: two boxes and a center merge on cream stage.

beats.narration_text: Say you're launching a new service. Research surveys the competitive landscape, finds the open gaps, and hands them to marketing. Marketing builds positioning into those gaps — a stance that stands apart, not another me-too voice.

shot.visual_intent: Competitor tiles arrange in a row across the stage; a terracotta highlight marks the open gap between them. Research box emits three finding-cards toward the gap. Marketing box receives them and its positioning block snaps into the gap.
shot.motion_claim: Finding-cards flow from research into an open gap; the marketing block fills it exactly — proving the hand-off produces targeted positioning, not generic messaging.

show.event: four competitor tiles arrive and arrange; gap between tiles two and three glows terracotta
research box emits three finding-cards moving toward the gap
marketing box lights; receives the cards
positioning block emerges from marketing box and snaps into the terracotta gap

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: competitor tiles, two domain boxes, and a gap fill on cream stage.

beats.narration_text: The same hand-off, aimed at a meeting. Research produces raw signals — recent news, hiring patterns, competitive position. Sales translates each signal into a move: your angle, the objections to expect, and what to lead with. Intelligence you can actually use.

shot.visual_intent: Research box emits three signal nodes labeled 'news', 'hiring', 'position'. Each node travels into the sales box. Three brief-move cards emerge from the other side of the sales box, labeled 'angle', 'objections', 'lead'.
shot.motion_claim: Signal nodes enter one side of the sales box and emerge as brief-move cards on the other side — showing translation from raw intelligence into actionable meeting moves.

show.event: research box emits three signal nodes: 'news', 'hiring', 'position'
first node slides into sales box
second and third nodes slide into sales box
three brief-move cards emerge from the right side of sales box
ink labels settle on cards: 'angle', 'objections', 'lead'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: two domain boxes with signal nodes and brief cards on cream stage.

beats.narration_text: Two more hand-offs share one shape. Performance data flows into the marketing calendar — built around what actually moved the needle. Support tickets flow into the product roadmap — you build against documented need, not what feels cool. Measurement feeds making, both ways.

shot.visual_intent: Two parallel cable paths on the stage. Left: a data box feeds a calendar box; data blocks flow along the cable. Right: a support box feeds a product box; ticket slips flow along the cable. Both paths complete and hold.
shot.motion_claim: Two parallel flows completing simultaneously — the identical shape of both hand-offs proves 'measurement feeds making' is the governing pattern, not a special case.

show.event: data box and calendar box appear; cable draws between them
data blocks flow left-to-right along the left cable
calendar assembles from blocks; ink label 'calendar'
support box and product box appear; cable draws between them
ticket slips flow along the right cable
roadmap assembles; ink label 'roadmap'
both completed paths hold; terracotta dot at each output end

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: two parallel cable paths on cream stage; the parallel structure is the idea.

beats.narration_text: Stack sales and legal on a contract and both blind spots disappear. Sales reads the relationship context. Legal reads the risk clauses. They merge into one negotiation brief — what to push on, what's standard, and where you're strong.

shot.visual_intent: A flat contract plate sits center-stage. Sales box floats above-left, legal box above-right. Each emits a stream that flows down and converges below the contract into a brief block labeled 'negotiation brief'.
shot.motion_claim: Two streams from opposite sides converging below one contract — proving that sales context and legal risk together cover what neither covers alone.

show.event: contract plate arrives at center-stage; ink label 'contract'
sales box appears above-left; emits relationship stream downward
legal box appears above-right; emits risk-clauses stream downward
both streams meet below the contract plate
brief block assembles; ink label 'negotiation brief'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: contract plate, two domain boxes, converging streams on cream stage.

beats.narration_text: Four habits keep combinations sharp. Name the domains you want — say them explicitly. Start simple and get fluent with one plugin before you orchestrate several. Document the combinations that work. Notice the gaps — they're signals for the next plugin to build.

shot.visual_intent: Four small labeled boxes drop in from above one by one and settle in a 2×2 grid: 'Name domains', 'Start simple', 'Document wins', 'Notice gaps'. Each lands as its habit is spoken.
shot.motion_claim: Four boxes landing and claiming separate cells — showing four discrete, ordered habits as a set you build one at a time.

show.event: 'Name domains' box drops into top-left cell
'Start simple' box drops into top-right cell
'Document wins' box drops into bottom-left cell
'Notice gaps' box drops into bottom-right cell
all four settled; terracotta dot on each lid

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: four labeled boxes in a 2×2 grid on cream stage.

beats.narration_text: When a two-plugin flow keeps earning its keep — research into outreach, say — write it down. Better: capture the whole workflow as a custom plugin. The whole sequence runs from one command.

shot.visual_intent: A research box and an outreach box sit connected by a cable with step marks. A token animates through the full flow. Then the two-box chain folds and compresses toward center into a single small command chip labeled 'one command'.
shot.motion_claim: Multi-step chain folding into one chip — proving a repeated two-plugin workflow becomes a reusable single command.

show.event: research box and outreach box appear with cable; step marks between them
token animates along the cable: research → outreach
chain begins folding and compressing toward center
single command chip materializes at center
chip settles; ink label 'one command'; terracotta dot on top

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: two-box chain compressing to a chip on cream stage.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Take one real move you're planning — a launch, a pitch, or a build. Name two domain plugins that could cover it from different angles. Ask Claude to work it from both, then show where the combined answer beats either angle alone. Then check two things. Does each domain contribute something the other couldn't? And is the hand-off explicit in your prompt, or are you hoping Claude guesses?

show.event: composer opens — 'Your turn.'
the prompt types in full
two check lines land

props.command: Take one real move you're planning — a launch, a pitch, or a build. Name two domain plugins that could cover it from different angles. Ask Claude to work it from both, then show where the combined answer beats either angle alone.
output: Check: each domain contributes something the other cannot.
Check: the hand-off is explicit in your prompt, not assumed.
